comments.body:
SOLVED on my end, got it working without re-installing.

Here is the steps I did:

1. remove wireguard
2. uninstall tailscale
3. clear programdata/tailscale
4. clear appdata/local/tailscale
5. reboot and reinstall tailscale

run tailscale -> issues still percists

1. close all instances of tailscale including the tailscale service
2. open powershell in admin
3. run tailscaled.exe

look for no access errors
if you have acess errors it might not have closed fully yet or you might need different premissions for the service.
(I setup mine to run as the local admin, most likely not needed)

NOTE: after you get it working if, you changed the permissions for it, remember to turn them back to "system" or it might not work after a reboot unless manually ran via powershell

if it runs with no "access denied" errors and you get something like this:

```
PS C:\Windows\system32> tailscaled.exe
logtail started
local disk logdir: C:\ProgramData\Tailscale\Logs
Program starting: v1.76.6-t1edcf9d46-gd0a6cd8b2, Go 1.23.1: []string{"C:\\Program Files\\Tailscale\\tailscaled.exe"}
LogID: ---
logpolicy: using dir C:\ProgramData\Tailscale
dns: using *dns.windowsManager
running ipconfig /registerdns ...
wgengine.NewUserspaceEngine(tun "Tailscale") ...
Installing driver 0.14
Extracting driver
WSL: found 2 distributions
Installing driver
Creating adapter
ran ipconfig /registerdns in 3.032s
running ipconfig /flushdns ...
ran ipconfig /flushdns in 16ms
Timed out waiting for device query: The wait operation timed out. (Code 0x00000102)
Failed to setup adapter (problem code: 0x1C, ntstatus: 0xC0000490): There was no match for the specified key in the index. (Code 0x00000491)
Installing driver 0.14
Extracting driver
Installing driver
Creating adapter
Timed out waiting for device query: The wait operation timed out. (Code 0x00000102)
Failed to setup adapter (problem code: 0x1C, ntstatus: 0xC0000490): There was no match for the specified key in the index. (Code 0x00000491)
```

then you can continue following the guide from here:
(https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/6461)

run these in an admin terminal or admin powershell

1. Export the list of drivers in the table form to a text file using the command:
dism /online /get-drivers /format:table > c:\drivers.txt

2. Find wintun or wireguard from the list, and note the "Published Name", oemNN.inf

3. Remove the driver using the command:
pnputil.exe /d oemNN.inf

(for me the actual wireguard driver was called: oem119.inf)

after this run tailscaled.exe again and it should now be able to install the driver 

if it install correctly close the powershell, remember to stop it first: ctrl+c
then start the service via the service manager

After this run the tailscale app like normal and login again, and it should now work as normal

comments.author: participant11
comments.body:
@participant14: You should not remove those files.

The script prints all NDIS notify object components installed on the device, both system and third-party.
These two are perfectly fine and aren't expected to cause any issues.

On some environments, the script may show warnings indicating that a component is still registered even though the corresponding .DLL file is missing. This usually happens due to incomplete or incorrect removal of third-party applications, such as VMware Workstation. Based on the script output, that's not the case here.

Additionally, some third-party components may contain bugs, but that's not the case on your environment either. The two listed files are well-known system components.

I'd suggest reaching out to <email-scrubbed>

for those that revo/bcu or any uninstaller or other solution didn't work, with the participant28 team, we found this in my machine:
```
!    sto:           Unable to determine presence of driver package 'oem63.inf'. Error = 0x00000020
     inf:           {Query Configurability: c:\windows\inf\oem63.inf} 23:56:37.028
```

We eliminate this driver, and participant28 started to work normally, the command `pnputil.exe /d oem63.inf`

I managed to fix this by

- Uninstall Tailscale
- Delete `C:\Program Files\Tailscale`
- Delete `C:\ProgramData\Tailscale`
- Delete `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Tailscale`
- Re-install Tailscale
